summary: Charles Rockwell Lanman was an Indologist and linguist who earned his B.A. at Yale and studied in Germany. He served as Sanskrit-Dozent at Johns Hopkins (1876–1880) and held a professorship at Harvard University from 1880 to 1926.

Charles S. Prebish is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Case Western Reserve University under David M. Miller and Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as Professor of Religious Studies at Pennsylvania State University (~1972–2007).

Charles Taliaferro is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Goddard College, the University of Rhode Island, Harvard Divinity School, and Brown University, later serving as a professor at St. Olaf College (~1985–2022).

Charles Taylor is a philosopher who studied at Selwyn House School, McGill University, and Balliol College, Oxford. His career includes posts at McGill University (~1961–1998), the Université de Montréal (~1962–1971), and Northwestern University (~2002–2014).

Charles Wei-hsun Fu worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Sinology. He studied at National Taiwan University (~1952–1959) and the University of Illinois System (~1963–1969), and held an academic post at Ohio University (~1968–1972).

Charles Wilkins was an Indologist and linguist who studied under the traditional teacher Kalinatha. He co-founded The Asiatic Society in 1784 and served as librarian for the East India Company, the India Office Library, and the India Office Records.

Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and Indology. He earned a doctorate in law at the University of Liège and held professorships at UCLouvain (from 1871) and KU Leuven (~1867–1899).

Chatral Sangye Dorje was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master. He studied under numerous traditional teachers, including Sera Khandro Dewé Dorje, Dorje Dradul, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, and Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang (~1931–1941), whom he later succeeded.

Chatsumarn Kabilsingh works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. She earned degrees from Visva-Bharati, McMaster, and Magadh universities, and served in the Department of Philosophy and Religion at Thammasat University (~1973–2000).

Chen-kuo Lin is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who completed his doctorate at Temple University in 1991. He served as Professor (attested 1997–1999) and Distinguished Professor (attested 2014–2018) at National Chengchi University.
Cheryl A. Crowley is a scholar of Japanology. She studied under Linda H. Chance, William R. LaFleur, Philip Boas Yampolsky, and Ryuichi Abe.
Chhimed Rigdzin Rinpoche was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teacher Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje. He held a post at Visva-Bharati University (attested 1997).

Chi Chen Ho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. She studied under traditional teacher Hsuan Hua, earned a Ph.D. at UCLA in 2010 under Robert E. Buswell Jr., and served as a teaching assistant there.
Chi-chen Wang was a Sinologist who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from ~1922 to 1924. He held a post at Columbia University from ~1929 to 1965.

Chi-chiang Huang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Arizona in 1986 under Jing-shen Tao, having also studied under Robert M. Gimello.
Chi-wah Chan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and Benjamin A. Elman, earning a Ph.D. at UCLA in 1993, and served as a teaching assistant at CUHK.
Chie Ikeya is a historian and archaeologist who studied under David K. Wyatt, earning a Ph.D. from Cornell University in 2006.
Chien Y. Hsu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under traditional teacher Zhenhua and under doctoral supervisors Leslie S. Kawamura and James B. Apple.

Chien-hsing Ho is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He has held positions as an Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Nanhua University (attested 2014) and at Academia Sinica (attested 2018).

Chih-mien Adrian Tseng is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned a Ph.D. at McMaster University under James A. Benn and became an Assistant Professor at Fo Guang University (attested 2016).
